title: US disables cargo ship leaving Iran in first confirmed blockade strike in a month
dek: US Central Command says an aircraft fired at the stern of the St Kitts-flagged M/V Huda after its crew ignored warnings. It says 147 ships have turned back since July and five have been disabled.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
US forces disabled a St Kitts-flagged cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman on Saturday after its crew ignored repeated warnings and tried several times to break the American naval blockade of Iran, US Central Command (CENTCOM) said. It is the first US strike on a merchant ship that the command has confirmed in nearly a month.

A US military aircraft "fired precision munitions at the stern" of the vessel, the M/V Huda, CENTCOM said in a statement late on Saturday, US time. The ship had made a port call in Iran and was trying to leave regional waters. The command said the crew had been told to leave the parts of the ship that were targeted before the strike. It gave no details of the crew's condition, their nationalities or the damage, and did not name the Iranian port.

## What happened

"U.S. forces continue to strictly enforce America's naval blockade against Iran," CENTCOM said. According to the command, 147 commercial vessels have been redirected since the blockade was reimposed in July after complying with US instructions, and five merchant ships that refused have been disabled. It said US forces had also destroyed 10 Iranian commercial oil tankers which it described as part of a "multibillion-dollar shadow network" run by Iran's Revolutionary Guards (IRGC). It advised mariners near Iran's coast to heed warnings from US forces.

The disclosure follows at least two cases in which the command did not announce strikes and declined to confirm them when asked, according to reports.

On Saturday evening, Iranian state media reported explosions on Qeshm Island, at the mouth of the Gulf, and in the port of Jask on the Gulf of Oman coast. The US military did not immediately respond, reports said. President Donald Trump had confirmed on Friday a strike on an Iranian air-defence system on Qeshm, which he called minor. Iran had not responded publicly to the strike on the Huda by early Sunday, India time.

## How the blockade works

The United States first imposed the blockade on 13 April, after war broke out between Iran and the US and Israel and Iran restricted traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. It was lifted in June after a deal between the two sides, and reimposed from 14 July. CENTCOM has said it covers the entire Iranian coastline and that any vessel entering or leaving the blockaded area without authorisation can be intercepted, diverted or captured.

In practice, most ships turn back when warned. Those that do not have been disabled from the air or the sea. In the first such case, on 19 April, a US destroyer fired into the engine room of the Iranian-flagged cargo ship Touska, which US Marines then seized, according to CENTCOM statements at the time. Since July, a Curaçao-flagged tanker, the Belma, was hit by missiles on its way to Iran's Kharg Island oil terminal; a Mozambique-flagged tanker, the Lavine, was disabled in the Gulf of Oman after what CENTCOM said were four attempts to break the blockade; and a Panama-flagged container ship, the Vela Nova, was disabled by a missile fired from a helicopter, according to the command's statements as reported at the time.

Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, has called the blockade an act of war. Lifting it is the first of Iran's conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, and it is the first step in the two-day plan that Qatar is pressing on both sides, according to reports.

## What they are saying

In Tehran, the IRGC spokesman, General Hossein Mohebbi, said on Saturday that the Guards had "surprises" ready if a third round of fighting began, and that Iran would be ready to change its nuclear doctrine "if the system concludes that it should move in that direction", according to reports. A day earlier he said Iran no longer considered itself bound by a 2,000-km limit on its missiles' range.

Iranian lawmakers hardened their tone. One MP, Abbas Golrou, said there should be no more talks until Washington meets Iran's demands, saying: "The Americans want to take everything and give nothing." Another, Ghasem Ravanbakhsh, threatened Saudi oil and water-desalination plants, and Britain, if they joined any attack, and said more than 40 MPs had signed a motion to impeach Mr Araghchi, according to reports. The motion's status could not be confirmed.

The diplomacy has not stopped. Mr Trump spoke to Qatar's emir, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, on Friday. The emir's office said they discussed "diplomatic efforts aimed at de-escalating tensions in the region" and that the emir stressed "continuing dialogue and relying on diplomatic means". US officials are divided between those who favour talks and those who favour more strikes, according to reports, and Iran is weighing Qatari proposals on nuclear questions it had earlier refused to discuss. Neither side has announced a deal.

## Why it matters for India

Indian seafarers make up a large share of the crews on merchant ships in the Gulf, and they have paid a heavy price in this conflict. The Ministry of External Affairs said on 3 November that 23 Indians, 15 of them seafarers, had been killed since the war began. The crew of the Huda has not been identified.

An Iranian lawmaker said this week that Indian ships are exempt from Iran's own restrictions on Hormuz traffic, a claim New Delhi has not confirmed. Any such exemption would not cover the US blockade, which applies to ships calling at Iranian ports whatever their flag. India buys most of its oil and gas from the Gulf, and every escalation at sea adds to freight and insurance costs for Indian importers. The Indian government has not commented on Saturday's strike.

## What happens next

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is due at a meeting of G7 foreign ministers in Paris on Monday and Tuesday, where the war and the blockade are expected to be discussed. Qatari mediators are trying to keep their plan alive, and Iran says it will not fully reopen the strait until the blockade is lifted. CENTCOM has given no sign that it will ease enforcement while talks go on.

## Key numbers

- 147: commercial vessels redirected since July, according to CENTCOM
- 5: merchant ships disabled for refusing to comply, the Huda among them
- 10: Iranian oil tankers CENTCOM says US forces have destroyed
- 13 April: the day the blockade first took effect; it was reimposed on 14 July
- 23: Indians killed in the West Asia conflict, 15 of them seafarers, according to the MEA (3 November)
